def densest_subgroup(n, edges):
    """
    Given a simple undirected graph with n vertices (labelled 0..n-1) and an
    edge list, consider every nonempty subset S of the vertices.  The density
    of S is |E(S)| / |S|, where E(S) is the set of edges with both endpoints
    in S.  Let D (a rational number) be the maximum density over all nonempty
    subsets S.

    Among the subsets achieving density D, the union of any two again
    achieves density D, so there is a unique inclusion-maximal subset U of
    density D.

    Return a tuple (p, q, k) of ints, where p/q equals D in lowest terms
    (q >= 1, gcd(p, q) == 1) and k == |U|.

    Input domain:
      1 <= n <= 40.
      edges is a list of pairs (u, v) with 0 <= u < v <= n-1; no pair appears
      twice; the pairs may be listed in any order; len(edges) may be 0.

    Edge case: if edges is empty every subset has density 0, so the answer is
    (0, 1, n) (U is then the whole vertex set).

    The answer must be exact (no floating-point answers).  Enumerating all
    2^n subsets is hopeless at n = 40; a correct solution must run in well
    under 0.1 s in CPython on every input in the domain.

    >>> densest_subgroup(3, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2)])
    (1, 1, 3)
    >>> densest_subgroup(5, [(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3), (3, 4)])
    (3, 2, 4)
    >>> densest_subgroup(6, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2), (3, 4), (4, 5), (3, 5)])
    (1, 1, 6)
    """
